answer: Sybil resistance derives from binding each agent identity to a remotely verified MRENCLAVE and a hardware-rooted, non-exportable attestation key, rather than to a software-only token. Identical enclave code may share a measurement, so the protocol must also enforce its identity policy against hardware-backed credentials; duplicating a VM cannot duplicate those keys. An attacker must obtain and attest additional physical silicon, not simply wander across virtual machines; each verified vertex rests on a hardware root, not timber-thin software claims.
